notable_absence.finding: No Enterprise/Community edition badges and no server-version-string citations anywhere on this page - both known recurring anomalies absent. The only gating axes on this page are capella-role:* (project-scope, disjunctive Project Owner/Cluster Manager) and billing plan (paid-plan-only for Advanced credentials/access roles), consistent with cluster-rbac.json's own account.

cross_component_finding: This page is a pure task/procedure page for the credential and access-role model cluster-rbac.json defines - it adds no new roles, privileges, or credential types, just UI/API procedures (create/edit/delete credentials, create/edit/delete access roles) plus a Hashicorp Vault integration note. Its Prerequisites section cites the SAME disjunctive project-scope pair (Project Owner, Cluster Manager) as allow-ip-address.md and (as read ahead) manage-buckets.md/scopes-collections.md, but conspicuously omits Organization Owner from that specific list - unlike allow-ip-address.md, which names all three. This is the first page in the batch where the Organization Owner->Project Owner impliesRole shortcut is NOT restated inline; a reader would need to already know (from manage-buckets.md or project-roles.md) that Organization Owner implies Project Owner access to know they qualify.
cross_product_finding: None new - reinforces cluster-rbac.json's finding that the credential/access-role/privilege model is entirely orthogonal to server/'s RBAC naming beyond the privilege-to-server-role mapping already covered on cluster-rbac.md itself; this page never names a Couchbase Server role directly.
